A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GREATER research work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack and defense experiments, including Tables 1–2, backbone evaluations in Table 5, and component ablations in Table 6.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds surrogate comparisons, training ablations, multilingual evaluations, and attacks on additional detectors.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 and Algorithms 1–3 retain the same token scoring, embedding perturbation, greedy search/pruning, losses, and alternating training procedure. Alternative surrogates and the frozen-adversary control are evaluations of the existing method.

E1.justification: v2 adds an M4 surrogate-training condition in Section 6.3 and explicit German and Urdu detection evaluations in Appendix B.4. These expand data and language coverage beyond the retained experiments; full-language detection differs from v1's word-level code-switching tests.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds RADAR and OUTFOX as defense competitors and HMGC and T-PGD as evaluated attacks. HMGC and T-PGD already appeared in Table 2, but their participation in the defense comparison is new. OUTFOX is evaluated only against text perturbations.

E3.justification: New evaluations introduce crossed surrogate-model/data conditions, a static-adversary control, a 200-query limit for GPTZero, and accuracy/F1 evaluation for multilingual detection. The original 8000/1000/1000 split, learning rate, and six-epoch training setting remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds surrogate/data sensitivity analysis, a synchronous-update ablation, epoch-by-epoch training analysis, and attack generalization tests on commercial, zero-shot, and decoder-only detectors. The earlier backbone study and component ablations are retained; the backbone study moves into Section 6.2.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added epoch trajectories describe training dynamics rather than independent repeated trials.

E6.justification: Expanded Table 1 changes GREATER-D's aggregate ASR from 5.75% to 5.53% under broader attack coverage; retained per-attack scores and Table 2 remain unchanged. New results include 34.08% versus 3.45% ASR without/with synchronous updates and 100% attack ASR on GPTZero. Table 13 adds case-specific perturbation and query counts.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, Definitions 1–3, Theorems 1–3, and their proofs are unchanged. The theoretical appendix moves from Appendix D to Appendix E without substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction narrow the claimed ASR advantage from 10.61 to 0.67 percentage points and expand claimed validation from 14 attacks and eight defense competitors to 16 attacks and ten competitors. The central framework and attack-efficiency contributions remain the same.

C2.justification: Section 6.3 newly interprets performance as insensitive to surrogate architecture/training data and argues that shared model families do not leak crucial information. New appendix discussions extend applicability claims to multilingual and additional detector settings. The original three substantive limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The v2 abstract adds a code-and-dataset repository link. New experiments specify surrogate/data combinations and the GPTZero query cap, while Appendix A.2's original hardware, implementation settings, and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds positioning against RADAR and OUTFOX, describing their focus on known attacks. References to M4 and Binoculars support the added evaluations. The broader related-work narrative and claimed research position are retained.

P1.justification: v2 moves the backbone discussion from Appendix B.2 to Section 6.2, adds discussion and appendix subsections plus acknowledgments, and makes limited grammatical corrections. Most existing exposition remains intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains comparator columns and attack rows, six new result tables are added, and the backbone table moves into the main text. The case-study table gains perturbation-rate and query-count columns. These substantially expand the tabular presentation; Figures 1–4 are retained.

improvement.justification: The new synchronous-update ablation and surrogate/detector generalization tests address gaps in v1's support for central claims, while RADAR and OUTFOX strengthen comparison coverage. However, the headline 0.67-point advantage compares GREATER-D's all-attack average with OUTFOX's text-perturbation-only average, and Section 5.1 misattributes OUTFOX's 6.20% to RADAR. These reporting defects temper the otherwise positive evidential gains.
